value: When is the major overhaul of a reciprocating engine a major repair that a powerplant mechanic may not approve for return to service?
reason: The handbook sentence is garbled and the card turned it into a limit on performing the work; 14 CFR 65.81(a) lets a mechanic perform or supervise it. What changes is approval: splitting such a crankcase is a major repair (part 43 appendix A), which 65.87(a) excludes.

value: When the engine has an integral supercharger or propeller reduction gearing other than spur-type: splitting its crankcase is then a major repair.
reason: As above: rests on 14 CFR part 43 appendix A (b)(2)(i)-(ii).

value: Section 65.87 of the regulations lets a powerplant mechanic approve for return to service only work that excludes major repairs, so such an overhaul needs someone with wider authority.
reason: Says why, from 14 CFR 65.87(a).

value: 14 CFR part 43, appendix A, paragraph (b)(2) (eCFR, current)
reason: Rule source replaces the ambiguous handbook sentence.

value: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/part-43#p-Appendix-A-to-Part-43(b)(2)
reason: Matches the new source.

value: Separation or disassembly of a crankcase or crankshaft of a reciprocating engine equipped with an integral supercharger.
reason: Words of part 43 appendix A (b)(2)(i).

value: A powerplant mechanic finishes a major overhaul, crankcase split, of an engine with an integral supercharger. Who may approve the engine for return to service?
reason: Keyed answer "No, a mechanic may not perform or supervise it" contradicts 14 CFR 65.81(a); the limit is on approval for return to service (65.87(a), 65.95(a)(1)).

value:
A) The powerplant mechanic who did the work
B) Any certificated mechanic who inspects it
C) A holder of an inspection authorisation, if approved data were used
D) The aircraft owner
reason: New options for the corrected question.

value: C: A holder of an inspection authorisation, if approved data were used
Splitting the crankcase of an engine with an integral supercharger is a powerplant major repair, and approving major repairs is an inspection authorisation privilege.
reason: Says why, from part 43 appendix A and 65.95(a)(1).

value: A is wrong: Section 65.87 of the regulations lets a powerplant mechanic approve only work that excludes major repairs. B is wrong: the same limit binds every mechanic, whoever inspects the work. D is wrong: an owner has no authority to approve maintenance for return to service.
reason: Matches the new choices; letters checked.

value: A is wrong: that is one cylinder only. B is wrong: 100 adds the bore area to one cylinder’s volume (80 + 20) instead of multiplying by four cylinders. D is wrong: that uses two cylinders.
reason: "Adds instead of multiplying" did not show how 100 arises.

value: B is wrong: that divides the wrong way round. C is wrong: 20 is the shortfall in cubic inches, not a percentage. D is wrong: that is the shortfall as a percentage.
